item_content: (S) Store HACCP plan is approved and maintained in store.

(S) Maintain a valid business license, food service license, hygiene permit, and any other licenses as required by local regulatory authorities. All licenses must be kept up to date and within their validity period. Operating without the required licenses is strictly prohibited.
The store shall display the business license and food service license/hygiene permit as required by the regulatory authorities.

[Temporary Deviation Waiver] The store is currently operating under New York City’s 22-day no-inspection grace period. The food establishment permit has not yet been obtained and remains pending, subject to approval by the Department of Health (DOH) following the required inspection.

(S) For each store, the person in charge (PIC: Store manager, assitant store manager or shift supervisor) should hold valid practice certificates in accordance with local regulations, such as the NYC Food Protection Certificate and carry a physical copy on-site.

Maintain inspection reports issued by government regulatory authorities for the current year. In the event of any identified non-conformities, appropriate corrective actions shall be taken, and timely communication shall be conducted with the relevant responsible departments to ensure resolution and compliance.

Do not open or tamper with any samples that have been sealed or retained by the regulatory authority.
 Ensure that the items and quantities recorded are consistent with those sealed or sampled by the authority, as per official documentation or sampling notice.

(M)Employees must not engage in food preparation, handling, or service if they have experienced any of the following symptoms or medical conditions within the past 48 hours:
a. Diarrhea
 b. Vomiting
 c. Fever
 d. Any other illness that may pose a risk of foodborne transmission (e.g., sore throat with fever, jaundice, or persistent coughing)

(M)Employees must not wear accessories or false eyelashes while working in food preparation or processing areas, as these items may pose a risk of physical contamination and hinder effective hand and face hygiene.                           No jewelry is allowed on the hands or forearms, including watches, bracelets or wrist 
bands, except for one ring in the form of a plain band without stones or etchings and medical bracelet with Doctor's note. 
Other jewelry must not be distracting. One small facial piercing no larger than a 
dime is allowed. Earrings or ear gauges must be no larger than a quarter. Necklaces, 
including medical alert necklaces, are allowed and must be worn under clothing. No other visible pierced jewelry or body adornments are allowed, including tongue studs 
and subdermal implants. 
Allowable jewelry must be simple in design and not be a health or safety hazard.

Nails should be clean, well-manicured and of short or moderate length. Nail polish or 
artificial nail coverings of any type are not permitted in the interest of food safety.
Employees must be dressed in clean and neat clothing in accordance with standard operating procedures, free from any odors or other potential sources of product contamination.
Beards and hair must be neatly trimmed and properly restrained to prevent contamination. Hair that extends beyond shoulder length must be securely tied back, braided, or covered with a hairnet.

Eating, drinking, chewing gum, and using any tobacco products—including smoking or snuff—are strictly prohibited in food preparation and food-contact areas to prevent contamination and ensure food safety.

Store personal belongings only in designated areas. Do not bring personal items into food storage or processing areas. The use or storage of glass, porcelain, or other fragile personal items in these areas is prohibited.

Store must clearly post a 'No Pets' sign on the window or door. Live animals are strictly prohibited from being brought into or kept in the store, except for service animals accompanying customers as permitted by law. All service animals must be properly controlled and must not pose a contamination risk.
(M) Wounds on hands and wrists must be properly covered with a blue bandage, and disposable gloves must be worn during any food-contact operations to prevent contamination.
Ensure availability of disposable gloves and maintain a supply of blue bandages for proper use as required.
Store unpacked disposable gloves in a clean, designated area, separate from non-food-contact materials to prevent contamination.
(M)Don’t touch the food or contact the food surface with bare hands or open the paper bag by blowing into it

(M) Employees must wash their hands before preparing food; after using the restroom; after coughing, sneezing, or blowing their nose; when changing tasks (e.g., from handling raw food to ready-to-eat food); and after any activity that may contaminate the hands (e.g., cleaning, taking out trash, handling money). Hands and wrists must be washed thoroughly with soap and warm running water for at least 20 seconds, following proper handwashing procedures to prevent cross-contamination and ensure food safety.
Employees must follow the established hand washing and sanitizing procedures to ensure food safety and prevent contamination.
(S) Use and store only food, food-contact packaging materials, supplies, and chemicals approved by Luckin Coffee. Do not use or store utensils or equipment that pose a high risk of contamination.

(M) Use and store only equipment, food-contact utensils and tools, disposable gloves, plastic wrap, ziplock bags, sealing stickers, water filtration systems, and other chemicals that are approved by Luckin Coffee.
Use and store only Non-food-contact utensils/tools, brand-related materials, and other items that are either approved or distributed by Luckin Coffee.

Do not store food and packaging materials in wet, splashing, or dirty areas that may lead to contamination. Additionally, keep food and packaging materials separate from cleaning supplies, waste, maintenance tools, and other non-food-contact items.
Store food, packaging materials and food contact utensils at least 6 inches off the ground.

Place all cream chargers (N₂O Cartridges) in a locked storage box. Only the Store Manager (SM), Assistant Store Manager (ASM) and Shift Supervisor (SS) are authorized to access and distribute cream chargers.
Once a cartridge is used up, a new one may be issued (“one in, one out” policy). The access code to the locked box is known only to ASM level and above. Cream chargers must not be stored at the front counter.
First aid supplies must be stored in a designated area. Employees' personal medicines must be secured in their own locker.
Do not store food-contacting tools and utensils together with non-food-contacting items.
Store food-contacting tools and utensils in a clean environment or container that is protected from contamination and free of standing water.
Ensure that food-contacting tools, utensils, and their food-contact surfaces are properly maintained, and pose no food safety hazards.
(S) Ensure that no cross-contamination or significant hazards occur during food processing.
Ensure that containers and equipment used for storing raw materials are properly covered when not in use. Do not stack containers without appropriate protective barriers.
Immediately cover the ice machine’s cover plate or ice bin after use. When handling or delivering ice, employees must wear disposable gloves and hair restraint in accordance with hygiene standards.
Store raw materials on the counter surface properly to prevent moisture accumulation and clumping.

Ensure that the handles (the part designed for holding and operating the tool or utensil) of food-contact tools and utensils do not fall into containers holding raw materials or come into direct contact with food.
Seal unpacked food and food-contacting packaging materials according to SOP; store unpacked food in closed containers or cabinets.
Ensure that the surfaces of food and packaging materials are clean and free from any risk of contamination.

Do not mix different categories of raw materials under any circumstances. This includes both direct mixing (e.g., storing different ingredients in the same container) and indirect cross-contact, such as using the same measuring spoons, scoops, or utensils across different ingredients. Separate tools, containers, and storage areas must be used to prevent contamination and maintain ingredient integrity.

The reuse of disposable gloves is strictly prohibited. They shall be replaced immediately upon contamination, including any contact with non-food-contact surfaces or other potential sources of contamination.
(S) Ensure that no foreign objects are present in the food served to customers and that raw materials used for food preparation are free from foreign contaminants.
(M) Ensure that raw materials used in food preparation are free from any foreign objects.
Identify hazards related to foreign object contamination in products.

Make sure there are no wooden boards, tools, or cleaning supplies in the food prep or back area unless they are treated to resist moisture and mold. Do not use any glass, ceramic, or other breakable utensils in these areas.

(M) Dishwashing and ware washing. All utensils, and equipment must be cleaned and sanitized manually or by machine using either heat or chemical method. Manual washing and sanitizing. A three compartment sink must be used when washing and sanitizing. All compartments of the sink must be large and deep enough to permit complete immersion of the largest equipment and utensils to be washed. Items must be: (1) Washed in the first compartment in a detergent solution; (2) Rinsed free of such solution in clean hot water in the second compartment; and (3) Sanitized in the third compartment with hot water or a chemical solution.

(M) Make sure cleaning and sanitation chemicals are available; Do not mix use different colored wipe for the designated area.                       Red— Food contact surfaces
 Green — Food handling (non-food contact)
 Blue — Customer seating area
 Yellow — Restroom (except toilet/urinal)
 Disposable wipe — Toilet/urinal only
Properly label the handwashing sink, washing sink, rinsing sink, and sanitizing sink according to the store’s standards, and ensure they are used correctly following store procedures.
(M) Prepare sanitizer at a concentration of 100 PPM, in accordance with the SSOP.

Provide cleaning and sanitizing supplies, tools, and equipment, and store them in a designated area away from food storage and preparation zones. Keep all items clean and in good condition. Immediately dispose of dirty water from mop buckets, and never use mop buckets to hold garbage or food-contact tools and utensils.
Wash and sanitize tools and utensils following standard procedures. All food-contact utensils and tools must be air-dried after washing and sanitizing.

Store cleaning cloths in designated containers, ensuring they are free of visible stains. Do not mix different types of cloths or use them without proper sanitization. Keep both the cleaning cloths and the sanitizer container clean and free of stains or residue, and ensure the cloths are fully immersed in the sanitizer solution at all times.

The dishwasher shall reach a final rinse temperature of 180°F before using each day. A photo of the temperature display must be taken and uploaded to Workstation as daily verification.
Once per week, a 180°F temperature strip shall be used during a wash cycle to confirm proper temperature. A photo of the strip result must be taken and uploaded to Workstation for weekly verification.
Keep the cleaning cloths and sanitizer container clean and free of stains or residue, and ensure the cloths are fully immersed in the sanitizer solution.
Ensure the single screen display/timer functions properly and employees operate it according to the requirements.
Ensure that the surface of tools and utensils are clean and free of food residues and limescale
Ensure that storage equipment is clean, in good condition, and free of food residues or dust.
Clean production-related equipment and accessories according to the standard, and keep them clean
(L) Keep food-contact surfaces and non-food-contact operation stands clean and free of limescale and standing water.

item_content: (L) Ensure there is no significant limescale buildup or standing water on the floor and around floor drains or drainage channels; promptly remove any fallen materials, packaging, decorative debris, and similar waste.
(L) Keep walls and windows free of stains, debris, etc.
(L) Keep ceilings, lights, and air vents in food processing and storage areas under 12 feet high clean and free of dust, limescale, condensation, etc.
(L) Ensure store pipes and drains are clean: Verify that water supply pipes, sewers, grease traps, and residue traps show no visible limescale buildup, odors, or mildew.
(L)Ventilation system are provided and properly installed to prevent excessive build-up of grease, heat, steam condensation vapors, odors, smoke and fumes.

(L) Use covered trash cans with securely fitting lids; ensure trash cans are free from damage or malfunction. Line trash cans with appropriate plastic liners to prevent leaks from torn or damaged bags containing waste.
(L) Trash cans must be cleaned immediately to prevent overflow or spillage. Ensure all trash containers are leak-proof, odor-free, and do not contain torn or damaged garbage bags.
(L) Garbage bags must be securely sealed and discarded in the designated disposal area. Bags should be intact and free from any leaks, tears, or spillage.

Trash must be separated into three categories: general trash (including waste that cannot be recycled or composted, as well as some recyclable containers that will be sorted by the waste company), compostable trash (such as coffee grounds), and recyclable trash (paper and cardboard). Each trash bin must be clearly labeled to indicate the type of waste it contains—landfill, compost, or recycle.
Hazardous waste, such as chemicals, batteries, fluorescent bulbs, or contaminated materials, is clearly identified and securely stored in designated place.
(L) Ensure all surfaces below 12 feet in the customer area—including floors, walls, windows, ceilings, lights, and sunshades—are clean and free of dust, buildup, and cobwebs.
(L) Keep signboards, LOGO, publicity boards, etc. of the store clean and well-maintained, and free of damage

(L) Maintain cleanliness of the food premises and surrounding areas:
 Keep tables and chairs in the customer area tidy, clean, and free of miscellaneous items; promptly remove any trash from tables. Ensure the food premises and the area around the store are neat and orderly: items should be properly arranged with no obstructions or discarded materials present.

(L) Keep the exterior area of the store clean and tidy. The sidewalk in front of the store shall be kept free of garbage, spills, and debris at all times — including around tree pits, grass strips, and any obstructions. Cleaning responsibility shall extend up to 18 inches into the street from the curb, including the gutter area where trash and water commonly accumulate. During winter months, snow and ice shall be promptly cleared from the sidewalk and adjacent areas to ensure safe and unobstructed pedestrian access.

(L) Ensure restrooms are stocked with toilet paper, soap or hand sanitizer, a trash can, and either clean paper towels or a hand dryer. Maintain the restroom in a clean condition, ensure all toilet facilities function properly, and keep any sanitary equipment in good working order.
(L) Ensure regular restroom cleaning records are kept.
Ensure that the sensors of temperature monitoring devices are correctly positioned in accordance with relevant standards (in the warmest area of the refrigerator).

item_content:
(S) The following violations must not occur in the store:
1. Expired food, food-contact packaging, or sanitizing chemicals; any tampering with expiration date labels on food served to customers, including covering, altering, or removing labels.
2. Raw ingredients in refrigeration or freezer units that are past their labeled expiration dates.
3. Major issues with expiration date labeling in cold storage—for example, missing date labels on three or more product types or five or more individual items.
module_name: Product Procedures and Expiry Date Management

item_content:
(M) The following conditions must not be present in the store:
1. Missing expiration date labels on food stored in refrigeration or freezer units.
2. Unpackaged room-temperature items and foods stored in food containers that have exceeded their recommended shelf life.
3. Cleaning chemicals (including handwashing solutions, general cleaners, etc.) that are past their expiration date.
4. Significant issues with expiration date labeling on room-temperature unpackaged items and those in food containers (e.g., missing expiration labels on three or more types or five or more individual items).

item_content: No expiration date labels on unpackaged room-temperature items or those stored in food containers.

item_content: Do not replace the original expiration date label when adding new materials to existing products of the same category.
module_name: Product Procedures and Expiry Date Management

item_content: Use food according to the First In, First Out (FIFO) principle.

item_content: (M) Ensure that lights above food processing and storage areas, as well as inside display refrigeration units, are well-maintained, undamaged, and shatterproof.
Refrigeration and freezer temperatures meet standards: refrigeration between 32°F and 41°F, and freezing at or below 0°F.
Ensure refrigerators and other storage equipment operate properly and are well-maintained, free of dust, missing parts, damaged seals or racks, frost buildup, and freezing issues.
Ensure production equipment operates properly and is well-maintained, with no missing parts.
Ensure that sink stoppers, faucets, and the spray heads on the rinsing machine are in proper working condition.
(S) Do not store chemicals in food containers.
Store chemicals in designated secured areas away from food, food-contact surfaces, and packaging materials to prevent contamination or safety hazards.
Chemicals stored in spray bottles or containers must have proper labeling.
Ensure all chemical containers are properly sealed and used in accordance with operational standards.

(S) No extreme pest issues       Store shall be kept free of rodents, insects and other pests. If any live pests (such as rodents, cockroaches, or flies) are found anywhere in the store during inspection, the store will automatically fail the inspection.
(M) No severe pest issue
No general pest issues

Install fly light traps and ensure they are working properly; avoid using electric shock fly killers, electric fly swatters, or similar devices. Insect light fixtures should be installed at a height of 6 to 7 feet in locations away from strong light sources and air currents. Whenever possible, they should not be placed directly above food processing or storage areas.

Doors of street facing stores that connect to the outside must be equipped with air curtains or other pest prevention devices, and the air curtain should fully cover the entire doorway opening. Ensure the air curtain is operating properly, with airflow directed diagonally outward or vertically downward

Ensure that glue boards for mice and cockroaches are intact, clean, and free from collapse or excessive debris. Place mouse glue boards along walls or baseboards. Verify that insect glue boards are properly used and replaced before they become overloaded or lose effectiveness.

Store shall inspect storage areas at least once per week. Perform weekly checks of all pest control devices, including insect light traps, rodent glue boards, cockroach bait stations, and other monitoring tools. If you find sign of Severe pest infestation, report to operation manager.
Verify that pest control and prevention are performed by a licensed pest management company, and ensure all activities follow regulatory and company standards.

(M) Do not purchase or store pest control chemicals or rodenticides in the store, except for approved insect light glue boards.
Do not use any other prohibited pesticides (e.g. Rodenticides) inside the store.
The pest control service should be conducted by company approved pest control company according to the regulations.
Provide a layout indicating all pest and rodent control stations, and ensure that the number and locations of these control points match exactly with those shown on the approved pest control map.
Inspect storage areas at least once per month. Perform monthly checks of all pest control devices, including rodent glue boards, cockroach bait stations, and other monitoring tools.
For stores facing the street, keep doors and windows that connect to the outside closed, or install screens on those windows.

Ensure there are no gaps around walls, doors, windows, and where pipes pass through walls or ceilings by properly sealing all openings to keep pests out. All doors opening into the establishment from the outside shall be equipped with barriers such as anti-pest tension brushes or a space no larger than one-eighth of an inch to prevent entry of rodents.
No trash or debris that could attract pests or rodents is permitted within a 6-foot area surrounding the store.
No backflow or overflow is present in sinks

(M) No severe pest issue
No general pest issues

Install fly light traps and ensure they are working properly; avoid using electric shock fly killers, electric fly swatters, or similar devices. Insect light fixtures should be installed at a height of 6 to 7 feet in locations away from strong light sources and air currents. Whenever possible, they should not be placed directly above food processing or storage areas.

Doors of street facing stores that connect to the outside must be equipped with air curtains or other pest prevention devices, and the air curtain should fully cover the entire doorway opening. Ensure the air curtain is operating properly, with airflow directed diagonally outward or vertically downward

Ensure that glue boards for mice and cockroaches are intact, clean, and free from collapse or excessive debris. Place mouse glue boards along walls or baseboards. Verify that insect glue boards are properly used and replaced before they become overloaded or lose effectiveness.

Store shall inspect storage areas at least once per week. Perform weekly checks of all pest control devices, including insect light traps, rodent glue boards, cockroach bait stations, and other monitoring tools. If you find sign of Severe pest infestation, report to operation manager.
Verify that pest control and prevention are performed by a licensed pest management company, and ensure all activities follow regulatory and company standards.

(M) Do not purchase or store pest control chemicals or rodenticides in the store, except for approved insect light glue boards.
Do not use any other prohibited pesticides (e.g. Rodenticides) inside the store.
The pest control service should be conducted by company approved pest control company according to the regulations.
Provide a layout indicating all pest and rodent control stations, and ensure that the number and locations of these control points match exactly with those shown on the approved pest control map.
Inspect storage areas at least once per month. Perform monthly checks of all pest control devices, including rodent glue boards, cockroach bait stations, and other monitoring tools.
For stores facing the street, keep doors and windows that connect to the outside closed, or install screens on those windows.

Ensure there are no gaps around walls, doors, windows, and where pipes pass through walls or ceilings by properly sealing all openings to keep pests out. item_content: (S) Maintain a valid business license, food service license, hygiene permit, and any other licenses as required by local regulatory authorities. All licenses must be kept up to date and within their validity period. Operating without the required licenses is strictly prohibited.
The store shall display the business license and food service license/hygiene permit as required by the regulatory authorities.

Maintain inspection reports issued by government regulatory authorities for the current year. In the event of any identified non-conformities, appropriate corrective actions shall be taken, and timely communication shall be conducted with the relevant responsible departments to ensure resolution and compliance.

Do not open or tamper with any samples that have been sealed or retained by the regulatory authority.
 Ensure that the items and quantities recorded are consistent with those sealed or sampled by the authority, as per official documentation or sampling notice.

(M)Employees must not engage in food preparation, handling, or service if they have experienced any of the following symptoms or medical conditions within the past 48 hours:
a. Diarrhea
 b. Vomiting
 c. Fever
 d. Any other illness that may pose a risk of foodborne transmission (e.g., sore throat with fever, jaundice, or persistent coughing)

(M)Employees must not wear accessories or false eyelashes while working in food preparation or processing areas, as these items may pose a risk of physical contamination and hinder effective hand and face hygiene.                           No jewelry is allowed on the hands or forearms, including watches, bracelets or wrist 
bands, except for one ring in the form of a plain band without stones or etchings and medical bracelet with Doctor's note. 
Other jewelry must not be distracting. One small facial piercing no larger than a 
dime is allowed. Earrings or ear gauges must be no larger than a quarter. Necklaces, 
including medical alert necklaces, are allowed and must be worn under clothing. No other visible pierced jewelry or body adornments are allowed, including tongue studs 
and subdermal implants. 
Allowable jewelry must be simple in design and not be a health or safety hazard.

Nails should be clean, well-manicured and of short or moderate length. Nail polish or 
artificial nail coverings of any type are not permitted in the interest of food safety.
Employees must be dressed in clean and neat clothing in accordance with standard operating procedures, free from any odors or other potential sources of product contamination.
Beards and hair must be neatly trimmed and properly restrained to prevent contamination. Hair that extends beyond shoulder length must be securely tied back, braided, or covered with a hairnet.

Eating, drinking, chewing gum, and using any tobacco products—including smoking or snuff—are strictly prohibited in food preparation and food-contact areas to prevent contamination and ensure food safety.

Store personal belongings only in designated areas. Do not bring personal items into food storage or processing areas. The use or storage of glass, porcelain, or other fragile personal items in these areas is prohibited.

Store must clearly post a 'No Pets' sign on the window or door. Live animals are strictly prohibited from being brought into or kept in the store, except for service animals accompanying customers as permitted by law. All service animals must be properly controlled and must not pose a contamination risk.

Store unpacked disposable gloves in a clean, designated area, separate from non-food-contact materials to prevent contamination.
(M)Don’t touch the food or contact the food surface with bare hands or open the paper bag by blowing into it

(M) Employees must wash their hands before preparing food; after using the restroom; after coughing, sneezing, or blowing their nose; when changing tasks (e.g., from handling raw food to ready-to-eat food); and after any activity that may contaminate the hands (e.g., cleaning, taking out trash, handling money). Hands and wrists must be washed thoroughly with soap and warm running water for at least 20 seconds, following proper handwashing procedures to prevent cross-contamination and ensure food safety.
Employees must follow the established hand washing and sanitizing procedures to ensure food safety and prevent contamination.

Store food, packaging materials and food contact utensils at least 6 inches off the ground.

Place all cream chargers (N₂O Cartridges) in a locked storage box. Only the Store Manager (SM), Assistant Store Manager (ASM) and Shift Supervisor (SS) are authorized to access and distribute cream chargers.
Once a cartridge is used up, a new one may be issued (“one in, one out” policy). The access code to the locked box is known only to ASM level and above. Cream chargers must not be stored at the front counter.
First aid supplies must be stored in a designated area. Employees' personal medicines must be secured in their own locker.
Do not store food-contacting tools and utensils together with non-food-contacting items.
Store food-contacting tools and utensils in a clean environment or container that is protected from contamination and free of standing water.
Ensure that food-contacting tools, utensils, and their food-contact surfaces are properly maintained, and pose no food safety hazards.
(S) Ensure that no cross-contamination or significant hazards occur during food processing.
Ensure that containers and equipment used for storing raw materials are properly covered when not in use. Do not stack containers without appropriate protective barriers.
Immediately cover the ice machine’s cover plate or ice bin after use. When handling or delivering ice, employees must wear disposable gloves and hair restraint in accordance with hygiene standards.
Store raw materials on the counter surface properly to prevent moisture accumulation and clumping.

Seal unpacked food and food-contacting packaging materials according to SOP; store unpacked food in closed containers or cabinets.
Ensure that the surfaces of food and packaging materials are clean and free from any risk of contamination.

Do not mix different categories of raw materials under any circumstances. This includes both direct mixing (e.g., storing different ingredients in the same container) and indirect cross-contact, such as using the same measuring spoons, scoops, or utensils across different ingredients. Separate tools, containers, and storage areas must be used to prevent contamination and maintain ingredient integrity.

The reuse of disposable gloves is strictly prohibited. They shall be replaced immediately upon contamination, including any contact with non-food-contact surfaces or other potential sources of contamination.

(M) Ensure that raw materials used in food preparation are free from any foreign objects.
Identify hazards related to foreign object contamination in products.

Store cleaning cloths in designated containers, ensuring they are free of visible stains. Do not mix different types of cloths or use them without proper sanitization. Keep both the cleaning cloths and the sanitizer container clean and free of stains or residue, and ensure the cloths are fully immersed in the sanitizer solution at all times.
Ensure the single screen display/timer functions properly and employees operate it according to the requirements.

The dishwasher shall reach a final rinse temperature of 180°F before using each day. A photo of the temperature display must be taken and uploaded to Workstation as daily verification.
Once per week, a 180°F temperature strip shall be used during a wash cycle to confirm proper temperature. A photo of the strip result must be taken and uploaded to Workstation for weekly verification.

item_content: (M) Ensure that lights above food processing and storage areas, as well as inside display refrigeration units, are well-maintained, undamaged, and shatterproof.
Refrigeration and freezer temperatures meet standards: refrigeration between 32°F and 41°F, and freezing at or below 0°F.

Store chemicals in designated secured areas away from food, food-contact surfaces, and packaging materials to prevent contamination or safety hazards.
Chemicals stored in spray bottles or containers must have proper labeling.

(S) No extreme pest issues       Store shall be kept free of rodents, insects and other pests. If any live pests (such as rodents, cockroaches, or flies) are found anywhere in the store during inspection, the store will automatically fail the inspection.
(M) No severe pest issue
No general pest issues

Install fly light traps and ensure they are working properly; avoid using electric shock fly killers, electric fly swatters, or similar devices. Insect light fixtures should be installed at a height of 6 to 7 feet in locations away from strong light sources and air currents. Whenever possible, they should not be placed directly above food processing or storage areas.

Doors of street facing stores that connect to the outside must be equipped with air curtains or other pest prevention devices, and the air curtain should fully cover the entire doorway opening. Ensure the air curtain is operating properly, with airflow directed diagonally outward or vertically downward

Ensure that glue boards for mice and cockroaches are intact, clean, and free from collapse or excessive debris. Place mouse glue boards along walls or baseboards. Verify that insect glue boards are properly used and replaced before they become overloaded or lose effectiveness.

Store shall inspect storage areas at least once per week. Perform weekly checks of all pest control devices, including insect light traps, rodent glue boards, cockroach bait stations, and other monitoring tools. If you find sign of Severe pest infestation, report to operation manager.
Verify that pest control and prevention are performed by a licensed pest management company, and ensure all activities follow regulatory and company standards.

(M) Do not purchase or store pest control chemicals or rodenticides in the store, except for approved insect light glue boards.
Do not use any other prohibited pesticides (e.g. Rodenticides) inside the store.
The pest control service should be conducted by company approved pest control company according to the regulations.
Provide a layout indicating all pest and rodent control stations, and ensure that the number and locations of these control points match exactly with those shown on the approved pest control map.
Inspect storage areas at least once per month. Perform monthly checks of all pest control devices, including rodent glue boards, cockroach bait stations, and other monitoring tools.
For stores facing the street, keep doors and windows that connect to the outside closed, or install screens on those windows.

Ensure there are no gaps around walls, doors, windows, and where pipes pass through walls or ceilings by properly sealing all openings to keep pests out. All doors opening into the establishment from the outside shall be equipped with barriers such as anti-pest tension brushes or a space no larger than one-eighth of an inch to prevent entry of rodents.
No trash or debris that could attract pests or rodents is permitted within a 6-foot area surrounding the store.
No backflow or overflow is present in sinks

Trash must be separated into three categories: general trash (including waste that cannot be recycled or composted, as well as some recyclable containers that will be sorted by the waste company), compostable trash (such as coffee grounds), and recyclable trash (paper and cardboard). Each trash bin must be clearly labeled to indicate the type of waste it contains—landfill, compost, or recycle.
Hazardous waste, such as chemicals, batteries, fluorescent bulbs, or contaminated materials, is clearly identified and securely stored in designated place.

(a) Keep refrigerated foods 32–41°F and frozen foods ≤0°F.
(b) Monitor temperatures daily and keep records.
(c) All refridgerators must have 1 thermometer present.

(a) Refrigerated or frozen food: Do not hold at room temperature > 15 mins
(b) Hot food: hold≥135°F; max 15 mins outside temperature control.

item_content:
(S) Expiration Date Compliance:
(a) No expired food, packaging, or sanitizers; do not tamper with expiration labels; 
(b) Raw ingredients in fridge/freezer must be within expiration dates.
(c) Cold storage labeling: Missing dates on ≥3 product types or ≥5 items is a violation.

(M) Expiration Date Compliance:
(a) No missing expiration labels on refrigerated/freezer food.
(b) No expired or unpackaged room-temp items.
(c) No expired cleaning chemicals.
(d) Room-temp labeling: Missing dates on ≥3 types or ≥5 items.

(a) Label all unpackaged and container-stored foods with clear, accurate expiration dates.
(b) Do not alter, obscure, or replace original labels.
(c) Do not cover original expiration dates on thawed or opened products.
Use food according to the FEFO (First Expired, First Out) principle.

(a) Ensure storage and production equipment operate properly and are well-maintained.
(b) Storage Equipment must be intact, and free of frost or freezing issues.

(A) Out of service Equipment must have an out of service tag and ticket submitted. 
(B) Out of Service Equipement must not be used during production. 
(C) No Temporary Repair that poses any hazard should be allowed in store.

(a) Ensure water filtration system is functional.
(b) Keep the system well-maintained.
(c) Verify it has a valid service tag.
(M) Ensure that lights above food processing and storage areas, as well as inside display refrigeration units, are well-maintained, undamaged, and shatterproof.
Sinks should be fully operational with nothing broke and loose.

(a) Facility should be kept in good condition. (Example: Walls, windows, floors,doors,  no gaps or cracks, holes, signs of leakage, paint peeling, etc.) 
(b) Countertop gaps must be sealed to prevent collection of food residue.
No backflow or overflow is present in sinks or drains.

(a) Ensure pipes and drains are clean and free of limescale, odors, or mold.
(b) Ensure no leaks, and that pipes are well-maintained with joints properly sealed

(S)
(a) Ensure all plumbing and fixtures are properly connected, vented, and drained.
(b) Equip potable water systems with backflow prevention to prevent contamination.                   
(c) Wrap sewage pipes above food storage areas to prevent leaks. 
(d) Air gap: The vertical distance between the outlet and the flood level rim must be at least twice the diameter of the outlet pipe and not less than 1 inch.

(a) Keep drains and traps clean, clear, and odor-free.
(b) Ensure covers and filters are intact and leak-free.

(M) 
(a) Ensure the store has adequate potable water supplies.
(b) Install plumbing and fixtures properly to provide safe potable water to all areas.

(S) No extreme pest issues: Store shall be kept free of rodents, insects and other pests. If excess live rodents, cockroaches, or flies are found anywhere in the store during inspection, the store will automatically fail the inspection.

1. One or more live mice or dead bodies, except those on the sticky trap for mice
2. More than 2 live cockroaches                                             
3. Four or Five cockroach dead bodies
4. More than 20 live filth flies

(M) No severe pest issue
1. Feces of mice
2. One live cockroach
3. Three or four cockroach dead bodies
4. Serious live filth flies signs (more than 10 live flying insects and dead bodies, and may not easily result in customer complaints)

No general pest issues
1. Less than 3 cockroach dead bodies
2. General live filth flies signs (more than 5 live flying insects and dead bodies, and may not easily result in customer complaints)
3. Dead bodies of flying insects in the refrigerator, cup rack, bar mat and other high-risk areas
4. Situations in 9.1.1 & 9.1.2, but emergency disinfection worksheet has been initiated
5. Other pests activities

(a) Ensure pest control services are performed by a company-approved licensed provider.
(b) Pest Services must follow schedule.                     
(c) Keep service reports onsite.

(a) Install fly light traps and ensure proper operation.
(b) Do not use electric shock fly killers or swatters.
(c) Install 6 ft high, away from strong lights, ventilations, and not directly above food areas.
(M) Use only approved insect glue boards; no other pest chemicals or rodenticides in the store.

(a) Do not move traps from designated areas. 
(b) Replace insect light glue board before they become overloaded or lose effectiveness.  (Less than 2/3's full)

(a) Store shall inspect storage areas weekly.
(b) Check all pest control devices weekly (light traps, glue boards, cockroach baits, etc.).
(c) Report severe pest issues to the operations manager.
For street-facing stores, keep doors/windows closed or install screens.
(a) Street-facing doors must have air curtains fully covering the opening.                                          (b) Ensure the air curtain is operating properly. (Except in Winter)
(a)  Doors from outside must have barriers (e.g., tension brushes) or openings underneath≤1/8 inch.

(a) Non-public areas (e.g., preparation and storage areas) are restricted to authorized personnel only. Unauthorized individuals are strictly prohibited from entering food preparation areas.
(b) Visitors, vendors, and contractors must be supervised at all times while in non-public areas.
(c) Back doors and delivery entrances must be kept closed and secured when not in use.
(d) Surveillance cameras must operate continuously (24/7).

Receiving & Product Integrity 
(a)  Deliveries are accepted only from approved suppliers. 
(b) Products are inspected for tampering, damage, or broken seals upon receipt. 
(c) Suspicious or compromised products are isolated and reported

Awareness & Reporting 
(a) Staff demonstrate awareness of reporting suspicious activity
(b) Incidents or unusual situations are reported to management / QA.
Safety signs (e.g., “Hot Surface”) and caution labelsare visible and legible.
All walkways, doors, and stairways must be unobstructed, properly illuminated and meet safety requirements.

(a) Exit signs clearly display “EXIT”.
(b) Non-exit doors labeled “NOT AN EXIT,” “STOREROOM,” or similar.

(a) Electrical panels display warning labels and remain closed when not in use.
(b) Maintain clear access: at least 3 feet in front and panel width clear.

(a) Fire extinguishers are fully charged and accessible.
(b) Inspected annually by a certified company.
(c) Service tag shows monthly visual inspections by store employees.

(a) Maintain an Emergency Contact Plan with key personnel and local responders.
(b) Post emergency phone numbers in visible areas.

Prepare ingredients according to standard
1. Use correct ingredients and standard quantities.
2. Follow the required sequence, mixing method, and preparation time.
3. Add coffee beans and milk to the machine according to standard.

Prepare beverages according to standard
1. Use correct ingredients and standard quantities.
2. Mix according to standard and use the ice scoop correctly.
3. Follow the required sequence with no missing steps.

(S) Do not re-serve prepared beverages or purchased products
1. Do not re-serve items that have left camera coverage.
2. Prevent any other related food-safety risk.

Do not transfer ice or store ice in nonstandard containers
1. Do not transfer ice into or out of the store.
2. Do not purchase ice independently.
3. Store ice only in approved containers designed for safe ice storage.

Prevent contamination risks during operations
1. Protect food, ice, cups, lids, utensils, and food-contact surfaces from contamination.
2. Clean, rinse, cover, and store nozzles, utensils, steam wands, and containers correctly after use.
3. Use designated cloths, gloves, wound coverings, and tools only for their assigned purposes.

Wash and sanitize utensils according to standard
1. Follow the approved dishwasher or manual warewashing procedure.
2. Use approved sanitizer at the required concentration and contact time, with full surface contact.
3. Air-dry utensils completely and store them according to standard.

Prepare sanitizer according to the approved SOP
1. Mix 2 bags of Kay-5 with room-temperature water in a 5-gallon container.
2. Fill to the 5-gallon line, fully dissolve, and verify 100 ppm with a test strip.
3. Maintain required contact time and prepare a fresh batch when volume or concentration is inadequate.

Wash hands according to standard
1. Wash at scheduled prompt times within ±15 minutes when the store is open.
2. Wash at all required moments, including before food prep and after breaks, restroom use, contamination, coughing, or touching the face/hair.
3. Use soap and scrub all hand surfaces for at least 20 seconds.

Transfer ice according to standard
1. Wash hands and wear clear disposable gloves on both hands.
2. Sanitize the ice bin/cart, bucket, lid, and scoop before use.
3. Keep all ice-machine, bin, cart, and bucket lids closed promptly during transfer.

Do not leave refrigerated/frozen materials at room temperature beyond the limit
1. Keep refrigerated and frozen materials at room temperature for no more than 15 minutes.
2. Return prepared refrigerated materials immediately after use.

Follow the shelf-life labeling and use process
1. Apply the correct shelf-life label before opening, thawing, transferring, or preparing.
2. Do not overwrite, cover, misuse, or combine labels.
3. Do not extend shelf life by delayed labeling or by mixing old and new materials.

No missing shelf-life labels or retained expired materials
1. Do not leave opened or prepared items unlabeled for more than 15 minutes.
2. Do not retain expired materials.
3. Do not extend shelf life through delayed labeling, relabeling, or mixing old and new materials.
